walkthrough: Goal: draw on the tablet the way a hand really holds a pen: the side of the hand rests on the glass, strokes end where the ink ends, undo works, and the drawing is still there after the app was closed.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library: the dark top bar over the white canvas, and at the left edge the side bar with grey undo and redo arrows under its sliders.

Draw a curve with the pen and lift it. The ink follows the tip with pressure and ends in the brush's round tip right where the pen left the glass: no thin tail flicking towards the point the pen reported as it lifted.
Rest the side of the hand on the canvas, then draw a second curve. The resting hand leaves no mark and does not interrupt or bend the stroke; lifting the pen and then the hand changes nothing more.
Draw a third stroke while the hand brushes over the undo arrow and leaves it again before the pen lifts: the stroke is complete, nothing is undone, the arrow never reacts.

Let the hand lie on the undo arrow before the pen touches, draw a fourth stroke, lift the pen, then the hand: the moment the pen lands the hand's touch is dropped, so nothing is undone when the hand lifts.
Tap undo with a finger: the fourth stroke disappears. With the pen off the glass a finger is a finger again, so deliberate taps work.
Leave the app and let the system close it, open it again: the three strokes are there, undo is grey (history is not stored).
Failure: a touch the system itself cancels as a palm does nothing, even over a button. If the system cancels the pen's own contact, that stroke is dropped and the canvas shows the version before it.

Not here: telling a resting hand from a finger before the pen lands (a hand that taps a button and lifts before the pen touches counts as a tap); gestures such as two-finger undo; pen feel, which the author judges on the tablet.
